review_evidence: Item-by-item review for chapter alignment, age fit, stage progression, fresh independent and assessment passages, deterministic masterclass answers, and non-revealing prompts.
title: Come Back Soon
source_note: Aligned to the NCERT chapter title and themes of transport, distance, journeys, and returning. All Zidd passages, prompts, examples, and feedback are original.

levels.title: Pack the right travel details
levels.focus: find where a traveller goes and how the traveller moves
levels.teaching_goal: Separate destination, vehicle, and return details in short original travel plans.

guided_check.teaching_block: A travel sentence can tell us a place and a way to get there. Read the action first, then match each detail to the right question. If a place is chosen as a vehicle, reread the words after by.
guided_check.passage: Pihu visits the lake by bus and comes home before lunch.
guided_check.prompt: How does Pihu travel to the lake?

bridge.teaching_block: Now find two details without labels. Ask where? and how? before choosing. Do not let the nearest word replace the detail the question asks for.
bridge.passage: Kabir rides a train to Jaipur. His uncle meets him at the station.
bridge.prompt: Which pair gives the destination and the vehicle?

masterclass.teaching_block: Read the whole plan because the outward trip and return trip use different vehicles. Track the action named in the question.
masterclass.passage: Meera sails to the island on a ferry and returns on a small plane.

independent_check.teaching_block: Work without choices. Locate the reason before naming it; a time and a cause are different details.
independent_check.passage: Arun waited under the roof. The boat arrived late because thick fog covered the river.
independent_check.prompt: Why did the boat arrive late?
accepted_answers: the river was covered by thick fog

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same detail-finding skill in a school outing, not a family journey. Answer only what the question asks.
transfer_check.passage: Class 2 visits a pottery centre. The children cycle there in pairs and carry water bottles.
transfer_check.prompt: How do the children reach the pottery centre?

levels.title: Sort vehicles by where they move
levels.focus: classify familiar transport as land, water, or air travel
levels.teaching_goal: Use movement clues to group vehicles and explain a simple transport choice.

guided_check.teaching_block: Vehicles can move on land, on water, or in the air. Look at the surface in the clue. Wheels alone do not decide every answer.
guided_check.passage: A raft floats on a river while a truck rolls beside it.

bridge.teaching_block: Use the movement word as your clue, then name the group. Floating points to water; flying points to air.
bridge.passage: The helicopter rises above the hills to carry a doctor quickly.
bridge.prompt: Which transport group fits the helicopter?

masterclass.teaching_block: Some vehicles stop on land but travel elsewhere. Classify the place where the vehicle moves during the trip.
masterclass.passage: A ship leaves the harbour and crosses the sea overnight.
masterclass.prompt: Is the ship land, water, or air transport?

independent_check.teaching_block: Name the transport group without choices. Think about the track or surface named in the sentence.
independent_check.passage: A metro enters a tunnel and follows steel rails under the city.
independent_check.prompt: Which transport group does the metro belong to?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the sorting idea to a rescue scene. Classify the vehicle by where it travels.
transfer_check.passage: After the flood, a rescue canoe carries food across the village pond.
transfer_check.prompt: Which transport group does the canoe belong to?

levels.title: Use near, far, leave, and return
levels.focus: work out and use travel words from context
levels.teaching_goal: Infer simple distance and journey words from nearby time and place clues.

guided_check.teaching_block: Nearby words can show a travel word's meaning. A short walk suggests near; many hours suggest far. Check the whole clue, not only one number.
guided_check.passage: The clinic is near Ria's house, so she walks there in three minutes.

bridge.teaching_block: Compare the two places before deciding. The clue may show meaning through contrast.
bridge.passage: The park is close, but the fort is far and takes four hours to reach.
bridge.prompt: Which word means a long distance away?

masterclass.teaching_block: Time words can reveal whether a traveller is going or coming back. Follow the direction of movement.
masterclass.passage: Naman leaves home at eight and returns after the match at noon.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the result in the second sentence to infer the word. Give a short meaning, not a copied sentence.
independent_check.passage: The hill path was distant. We packed lunch because the walk would take most of the day.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply context clues to a delivery, not a holiday. Use the direction of the action.
transfer_check.passage: The baker sends a cart to the market. After selling the bread, the driver heads back to the bakery.

levels.title: Put a journey in a clear order
levels.focus: sequence travel events and build ordered sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Use time clues to arrange travel events from departure to return.

guided_check.teaching_block: A journey has an order. Begin with the event marked first, then follow the time words. If the ending comes first, check the time clues again.
guided_check.passage: First, Tara buys a ticket. Next, she boards the bus. At last, she reaches the museum.
guided_check.prompt: What happens after Tara buys a ticket?

bridge.teaching_block: When time words are missing, use what must happen before travel can begin. A vehicle cannot arrive after a passenger has already reached the place.
bridge.passage: Events: The train arrives. Dev gets on. The train leaves the station.
options: train arrives, Dev gets on, train leaves
Dev gets on, train leaves, train arrives
train leaves, train arrives, Dev gets on
accepted_answers: train arrives, Dev gets on, train leaves
the train arrives, dev gets on, the train leaves

masterclass.teaching_block: Follow both direction and time. The return event belongs after the visit, even if it is mentioned near the start.
masterclass.passage: Lina came home at five. Earlier, she toured the zoo after taking a taxi from school.
options: Lina took a taxi from school
accepted_answers: Lina took a taxi from school

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange the jumbled words into one clear sentence. Keep the doer before the action.
independent_check.passage: Words: crosses / the / blue / bridge / our / bus
independent_check.prompt: Write the sentence in the correct order.
accepted_answers: our bus crosses the blue bridge
our bus crosses the blue bridge.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use sentence order in a parcel-delivery context. Keep the time word at the beginning or end without changing the meaning.
transfer_check.passage: Words: at noon / reaches / the van / the bakery
accepted_answers: the van reaches the bakery at noon
the van reaches the bakery at noon.
at noon the van reaches the bakery
at noon, the van reaches the bakery.

levels.title: Write a useful travel message
levels.focus: write complete travel information for another person
levels.teaching_goal: Write concise messages that include the needed place, transport, or return detail.

guided_check.teaching_block: A useful travel message tells the key fact in a complete sentence. Include who, the action, and the needed detail. Do not add a detail that the note does not give.
guided_check.prompt: Which message gives Sana's plan clearly?
options: Sana will go to the library by auto-rickshaw at 4 p.m.
Sana likes books and yellow autos.
accepted_answers: Sana will go to the library by auto-rickshaw at 4 p.m.
sana will go to the library by auto rickshaw at 4 pm

bridge.teaching_block: Turn the travel card into one sentence. Check that the destination and return time both belong to the same traveller.
bridge.passage: Travel card: Omar - sports ground - bus - back by 6 p.m.
options: Omar will take a bus to the sports ground and return by 6 p.m.
The bus is large and the ground is green.
accepted_answers: Omar will take a bus to the sports ground and return by 6 p.m.
omar takes a bus to the sports ground and returns by 6 pm

masterclass.teaching_block: Select the message that is complete and accurate. A polished sentence must not invent a companion or change the vehicle.
masterclass.passage: Plan: Isha goes to the science fair by metro and comes back after lunch.
masterclass.prompt: Which message keeps every important detail correct?
options: Isha visits the science fair by metro and returns after lunch.
Isha and her cousin drive to the fair.
accepted_answers: Isha visits the science fair by metro and returns after lunch.
isha goes to the science fair by metro and comes back after lunch

independent_check.teaching_block: Write from a fresh trip card. Include the traveller, destination, vehicle, and return time. Any clear wording that carries all four details can succeed.
independent_check.passage: Trip card: Neel | bird park | bicycle | home by 11 a.m.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete message for Neel's family.

concept_slots.description: States that Neel goes to the bird park.
States that Neel travels by bicycle.
States that Neel will be home by 11 a.m.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer message writing to a library-book van. State where it will stop and when it will leave so readers can act on the notice.
transfer_check.passage: Notice facts: book van | community gate | arrives 3 p.m. | leaves 4 p.m.

concept_slots.description: Gives the community gate as the stop.

items.passage: Vani takes a taxi to the railway station. Her train goes to Agra.
items.prompt: Which vehicle takes Vani to the station?

items.passage: Rohit flies to Kochi and comes home on an overnight bus.
The school van stopped because a herd of goats was crossing the road.
accepted_answers: a herd of goats crossed the road

items.passage: Mili reaches the aquarium at ten. She leaves it after the dolphin show at noon.
A glider moves quietly through the air without an engine.
items.prompt: Which transport group fits a glider?

items.passage: The fishing boat carries baskets from one riverbank to the other.
A tram follows rails along a busy city street.
A seaplane rises from the lake and then flies above the coast.
items.prompt: Which group describes where it travels after rising?

items.passage: The kiosk is close enough for Aadi to reach it in two minutes.
The family began the return trip after sunset.
The village is remote, so the doctor travels for six hours to get there.
The passengers depart when the whistle sounds and the bus pulls away.
Words: slowly / the / ferry / moves / across / lake / the
accepted_answers: the ferry moves slowly across the lake
the ferry moves slowly across the lake.

items.passage: Words: our / at dawn / journey / begins
Events: We reach the platform. We buy tickets. We board the train.
options: buy tickets, reach the platform, board the train
reach the platform, buy tickets, board the train
board the train, buy tickets, reach the platform
accepted_answers: reach the platform, buy tickets, board the train

items.passage: Events: The bus leaves town. It stops at the fort. It returns to town.
Travel facts: Alia | cousin's farm | jeep | Sunday morning.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence about Alia's trip.

concept_slots.description: Gives the cousin's farm as the destination.
States that she travels by jeep.

items.passage: Journey note: Danish | planetarium | metro | returns after 2 p.m.
items.prompt: Write a message that keeps all four facts.

items.passage: A friend asks how to reach the reading club. Facts: take bus 8; get off at Rose Park; walk to the red gate.
items.prompt: Give the directions in one or two clear sentences.

concept_slots.description: Tells the friend to take bus 8.

any_of: leave the bus at rose park

concept_slots.description: Tells the friend to walk to the red gate.

items.passage: Return notice facts: art bus | school gate | leaves at 1 p.m. | everyone carries lunch.

concept_slots.description: Says that everyone should carry lunch.
